# Shortcut question: c7070676c606

**Question.** “For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed generator emits such cases.” [Question source](repo/REVIEW/questions/generator-shortcuts.json)

## Strongest plausible shortcut

**Count the blue cells in the top row, then recolor the k-th green object encountered from top to bottom.** This preserves marker counting while replacing size ranking with spatial order. It matches every usable canonical label:

| Canonical pair | Top-row marker count | Green sizes in discovery order | Selected size under both rules |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Train 0 | 2 | 5, 3, 2 | 3 |
| Train 1 | 3 | 6, 4, 3, 2 | 3 |
| Test 0 | 2 | 5, 4, 2, 3 | 4 |

Both rules use eligible four-connected green components. The intended rule sorts by descending cell count, then earliest occupied cell; the rival uses earliest occupied cell alone. Independent and declared rival implementations match all three canonical outputs. [Fresh fit evidence](checks/question/v3.0.4-generated-witness.json)

## Exact compact counterexample

This 10 × 10 input has two top-row blue cells and green sizes **3, 2, 4** in discovery order. Descending size order is **4, 3, 2**, so the three-cell L must turn red. The shortcut recolors the two-cell object. The lower blue cell does not contribute to k.

Each table entry is a complete row; coordinates are zero-based.

| Row | Input | Intended output, executed in Racket | `top_to_bottom` output |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 0 | `0110000000` | `0110000000` | `0110000000` |
| 1 | `0000000000` | `0000000000` | `0000000000` |
| 2 | `0330000000` | `0220000000` | `0330000000` |
| 3 | `0030000000` | `0020000000` | `0030000000` |
| 4 | `0003300000` | `0003300000` | `0002200000` |
| 5 | `0000000000` | `0000000000` | `0000000000` |
| 6 | `0000000000` | `0000000000` | `0000000000` |
| 7 | `0000000330` | `0000000330` | `0000000330` |
| 8 | `0000000330` | `0000000330` | `0000000330` |
| 9 | `1000000000` | `1000000000` | `1000000000` |

Racket changes `(2,1), (2,2), (3,2)`; the rival changes `(4,3), (4,4)`. This input also refutes bounding-box area, width, height, perimeter, eight-connectivity, global blue-cell count, and top-row blue-run count. [Retained fixture](repo/generators/c7070676c606/counterexamples/semantic_boundaries.json)

This fixture agrees with blue-component counting and second-smallest selection. Its distinguishing claim covers the original eight rivals.

## Does the final generator emit such cases?

**Yes, it emits this distinguishing family, although the literal 10 × 10 fixture is outside its declared width range of 11–24.** With no effective overrides, every even sample index uses `_rich`, varying padding, reflection, L-arm length, and singleton placement. Version 3.0.4 rich draws contain four or five green components and two isolated lower blue components. Odd default draws select one of their two smallest components, with descending rank other than 2; anchors use rank 3. Explicit overrides use the general sampler. [Final generator](repo/generators/c7070676c606/generator.py)

I generated and reference-checked this actual version-3.0.4 draw:

```python
generate(seed=0, sample_index=0, difficulty="easy")
```

It is **12 × 12**, with green sizes **3, 2, 1, 4, 1** in discovery order:

| Row | Actual generated input | Racket output | `top_to_bottom` output |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 0 | `110000000000` | `110000000000` | `110000000000` |
| 1 | `000000000000` | `000000000000` | `000000000000` |
| 2 | `003300000000` | `002200000000` | `003300000000` |
| 3 | `000300000000` | `000200000000` | `000300000000` |
| 4 | `000033000000` | `000033000000` | `000022000000` |
| 5 | `000000000000` | `000000000000` | `000000000000` |
| 6 | `030000000000` | `030000000000` | `030000000000` |
| 7 | `000000003300` | `000000003300` | `000000003300` |
| 8 | `000030003300` | `000030003300` | `000030003300` |
| 9 | `010100000000` | `010100000000` | `010100000000` |
| 10 | `000000000000` | `000000000000` | `000000000000` |
| 11 | `000000000000` | `000000000000` | `000000000000` |

Racket selects `(2,2), (2,3), (3,3)`; spatial ordering selects `(4,4), (4,5)`. All original eight rivals disagree, and `self_check` returns `[]`.

This draw also refutes `global_blue_components`: its **two top-row blue cells**, **four total blue cells**, and **three blue components** distinguish the counts. Blue-component counting selects green rank 3 and produces the same rival output shown above. Second-smallest selection also disagrees with Racket. [Exact pair and independent predictions](checks/question/v3.0.4-generated-witness.json)

## Verification and source bindings

The [reproduction script](checks/question/check_generated_witness_v3_0_4.py) imports the pinned generator, checks independent spatial, blue-component, and ascending-rank implementations, and runs the exact selected canonical program through one `ArcExecutor(use_racket=True)` bridge. All three canonical pairs and both counterexamples passed. Racket supplied every reference output; no runtime snapshot was copied.

| Subject | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| Final generator | `e9121bbc33924c5613c73f5c5194251c5a3999be33ee6f23791faccb8366efea` |
| Selected Racket rule text | `53d5f7ffc0796769cee4ded45f1ffa203b7c126b599754ad91e0b375bc349e5b` |
| Reproduction script | `66887a094b832d4165fd4681fbfd46bdbb1526e2172aed185eb84078e9e02b50` |

The [report](checks/question/v3.0.4-generated-witness.json) retains exact grid hashes, command, question hash, runtime identities, and confirmation that source bytes stayed stable. [Console receipt](checks/question/v3.0.4-replay.log)

## Limits of the claim

The lesson contract has **26 competitors: 16 fit all canonical pairs, while ten fixed-rank rules do not**. The nineteen distinguishing competitors comprise the original eight rivals, blue-component counting, and fixed ranks 1–5 counted from each end. Seven further canonical-fitting alternatives cover row-0 inclusion, clipping row 0 first, other colors, reversed ties, bounding-box tie breaks, dense ranks, and recoloring all tied objects. All seven agree on this generated witness; the claim does not require every lesson to refute them.

The observed blue-component rule exposed 31/300 production ambiguities and 122/1,200 ambiguous rotations on v3.0.2. [Retained rescore](checks/blue-components/FINDING.md) Fixed ascending ranks exposed 10/300 and 41/1,200 on v3.0.3; second-smallest alone accounted for 8/300 and 30/1,200. [Exact cases and rescore](checks/ascending-ranks/FINDING.md) Rich draws now target ascending rank 3 or 4, and odd draws target ascending rank 1 or 2. Explicit overrides and validation retain lawful ties.

The final [battery](checks/after-v3.0.4/result.json) passed **12/12 stages**. The [census](checks/lesson-census-v3.0.4.json) completed **300 three-demo lessons** and **1,200 required query rotations**, with **zero ambiguity** and **1,069 distinct inputs**. Each production lesson refuted nineteen competitors; seven agreed on all pairs. This replay measures three canonical pairs and two counterexamples; finite rival checks do not prove unrestricted rule identifiability.
